SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - APRIL 29, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made during regular business hours by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and the document(s) will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

7B.3. Approval of Fiscal Year 2023-24 Budget Amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Vo, to authorize administrative-initiated
  Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget amendments in accordance with Joint Budget Resolution No.
  2023-26 / CSA 2023-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget Preparation Policy
  (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project: 110-221-61325 Housing Services Program
  Amount: $90,000
  Justification: On June 22, 2023, the Cerritos City Council approved the expenditure of
  $50,000 of restricted Housing Asset Funds for the remediation of a City-owned
  affordable housing unit located at 19411 Pearl Court, Unit K, Cerritos, CA 90703, due to
  the uninhabitable conditions of the existing unit. The subject property is an affordable
  senior housing unit located within the Emerald Villas community, and is to be resold to
  qualifying moderate-income senior upon the restoration of the unit. During the
  commencement of initial remediation efforts and further inspection of the unit,
  unanticipated complications not within the project scope were identified, including the
  need for mold remediation. Due to the required mold remediation and mold inspections,
  and additional restoration work as a result of the poor condition of the unit, a budget
  amendment of $90,000 is being requested to restore the subject property to its original
  condition for resale to a moderate-income senior. It should be noted that the funding
  source for this allocation is the City’s restricted Housing Asset Fund, and no General
  Fund monies will be used for remediation purposes;

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.3. (continued)

  2. Account/Project: Gridley Park East Playground Refurbishment
  Amount: $420,000
  Justification: On Wednesday, November 1, 2023, the playground equipment and
  surfacing at Gridley Park East was burned down due to suspected arson. As a result, the
  remaining playground posts and subsurface were removed and must be replaced. The
  allocated funds will cover the costs associated with the refurbishment, including the
  acquisition of new playground equipment, new poured-in-place (PIP) surfacing,
  equipment and PIP installation, as well as the mandated post-installation audit.
  Documentation regarding the arson has been provided to initiate the insurance claims
  process. The City will seek reimbursement to cover the expenditures associated with
  this project;

  3. Account/Project: cp22207 Sheriff Station Patio Deck Refurbishment
  Amount: $78,000 (Transfer)
  Justification: Additional funding is required to complete the construction
  improvements for this project. The quote from the City’s on-call contractor to complete
  the necessary construction improvements exceeded the initial project budget. This
  increase is due to an overall rise in the cost of materials and labor. This amendment
  proposes a transfer of $78,000 from savings in other projects. Specifically, $62,000 will
  be transferred from cp14099 Arterial Street Block Wall Replacement and $16,000 from
  cp23212 Senior Center Roof Rehabilitation; and

  4. Account/Project: FY 2023-24 Mid-Year Budget Adjustment
  Amount: See below
  Justification: The Mid-Year Budget Adjustment is essential for aligning the City’s fiscal
  strategy with the evolving needs of the community and ensuring continued efficient
  operation of municipal services. Following a comprehensive review of all expenditures,
  revenues, and capital projects, adjustments have been identified to address variances
  from the initial budget assumptions. These adjustments reflect changes in revenue
  projections, modifications to expenditure accounts, and shifts in project timelines and
  costs. This consolidated amendment is proposed to facilitate streamlined management
  and oversight, ensuring that the budget remains a dynamic tool that accurately reflects
  the City’s priorities and financial reality. Details of the amendment have been provided
  in the agenda report associated with this item. A summary of the adjustments is shown
